title.value: SiT: Symmetry-Invariant Transformers for Generalisation in Reinforcement Learning
title.justification: The title explicitly mentions the proposed model 'SiT' and its application in generalizing reinforcement learning tasks, which is a core theme of the paper.
title.quote: We introduce Symmetry-Invariant Transformer (SiT), a scalable vision transformer (ViT) that leverages both local and global data patterns in a self-supervised manner to improve generalisation.

analysis.description: The paper introduces the Symmetry-Invariant Transformer (SiT), which is designed to improve generalization in reinforcement learning by effectively capturing and utilizing local and global symmetries. It refines traditional self-attention to preserve graph symmetries, leading to invariant and equivariant latent representations, demonstrating superior performance and efficiency over existing Vision Transformers on certain benchmarks.

type.justification: The study involves extensive experimentation and empirical evaluation of the proposed SiT model on various reinforcement learning benchmarks.
type.quote: We demonstrate the efficacy of SiTs over ViTs on prevalent RL generalization benchmarks, namely MiniGrid and Procgen, and show sample-efficiency on the the Atari100k and CIFAR-10 vision benchmark.

name.justification: The paper's primary focus is on improving generalization in Reinforcement Learning through the proposed model SiT, which is experimentally validated on RL benchmarks.
